summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, thrombotic microangiopathy, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, and a history of kidney transplant failure was admitted after two episodes of syncope at home, resulting in a nasal fracture and hip tenderness. The syncope was attributed to orthostatic hypotension likely due to dehydration from increased dialysis fluid and Miralax-induced diarrhea. She received 500cc IV fluids in the ED and was stabilized. Imaging showed a left nasal bone fracture without intracranial injury and a small, consolidated pericardial effusion without tamponade. Dialysis was adjusted, antihypertensives were temporarily held then restarted, and warfarin was changed to 3mg daily due to an elevated INR. The patient improved, remained stable, and was discharged home with plans for ENT follow-up, repeat echocardiogram in one week, and medication adjustments.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
